# Sīpa

> Sīpa sells one-of-a-kind statues, thangkas, Mithila paintings, and wood, stone and metal work made by named makers across Nepal. Every piece has a registry number for life (for example PTN-MT-26-0142). Makers are paid a fair share of every sale, enough to sustain their livelihood. Prices are set in Nepali rupees and shown in US dollars by default. Every piece ships cleared for export, with a printed catalogue card and a care kit for its material.

Key facts:
- A registry number has four parts: place made (PTN Patan, BKT Bhaktapur, KTM Kathmandu, JNK Janakpur, LMB Lumbini, PKR Pokhara), craft (MT metal, ST stone, WD wood, TK thangka, MH Mithila, PP paper and other), two-digit year finished, and a serial that is never reused.
- Anyone can check a number at https://sipa.example/registry. A record shows the piece, its maker, its registration date and its owners, named only with their consent.
- Placement guidance on Sīpa pages describes custom, not promises of luck or health.
- "Made in Lumbini" is used only for pieces made in Lumbini. Buddha figures made elsewhere in Nepal are described as "From the land of the Buddha's birth".

## Crafts
- [Lost-wax casting](https://sipa.example/crafts/lost-wax-casting): making metal objects from a wax model, a clay mould and molten metal, as practised by Newar families in Patan
- [Thangka painting](https://sipa.example/crafts/thangka-painting): mineral pigment and gold on cotton, drawn on a proportion grid
- [Mithila painting](https://sipa.example/crafts/mithila-painting): the folk painting of the Mithila region of Nepal and India, centred on Janakpur in Nepal
- [Newar woodcarving](https://sipa.example/crafts/newar-woodcarving): carved windows, doors, struts and pillars of the Kathmandu Valley
- [Stone carving](https://sipa.example/crafts/stone-carving): stone shaped by hammer and chisel into architecture, relief and figures

## Meaning
- [The mudras](https://sipa.example/meaning/mudras): the Buddha's hand gestures and what they mean
- [The earth-touching gesture](https://sipa.example/meaning/earth-touching-mudra)
- [Shakyamuni Buddha](https://sipa.example/meaning/shakyamuni-buddha), born in Lumbini, Nepal
- [The five Buddha families](https://sipa.example/meaning/five-buddha-families)
- [Green Tara](https://sipa.example/meaning/green-tara)
- [Ganesh](https://sipa.example/meaning/ganesh)
- [Mithila motifs](https://sipa.example/meaning/mithila-motifs): fish, peacock, bamboo, lotus, sun and moon
